raw_response:
My family has worked this land for three generations. I know Quzhou soil — flat, heavy clay loam, good if you water it right. My father grew wheat and corn, I grow wheat and corn. That's what this land is for, that's what the buyers want, and that's what I know how to do without making mistakes.

I have 12 mu. My son is in the city now, so I manage it alone, which means I keep it simple. Wheat in winter, corn in summer, same as every year, same as every neighbor.

For wheat, I sow in October. I buy seeds from the village supply cooperative — they sell the improved variety everyone uses, not the old ones my father grew. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then urea at jointing. I water four times: once before winter sets in, once in spring when it greens up, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in early spring and spray for aphids before harvest. I use the rotary tiller to prepare the seedbed.

For corn, I sow right after wheat harvest in June. I buy hybrid seed — everyone switched years ago, the yield is better. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the corn is knee-high. I water once if it rains enough, twice if summer is dry. I spray for corn borer once. After harvest I rotary till to chop up the stalks.

I apply what my experience tells me is enough fertilizer. I don't measure precisely — I go by what the bag recommends and add a little more to be safe. A bad harvest hurts. Wasted fertilizer I can live with.
